$Comment: The introduction to mastery: the Adventurer's Guide, standing in the Forgotten Temple, points
the player at the trainer a few paces away across the same landing. The quest exists to make
the player look up and notice them.
Npc.ViewId names the guide's temple id, so the guide is who OFFERS it: it appears on their
quest list down in the temple, right after the meeting that brought the player there. The step
names the trainer's role id instead, so the errand is taken from one character and discharged
at another. That placement authors no Identity.NpcId, so the character IS the role, and any
other standing of Mmo_Mastery_Trainer credits the step just as well.
There is no TurnInId, so the quest finishes on the trainer's conversation rather than on a walk
back to the guide; the reward sits in the Claim bucket and waits in the quest log until the
player collects it, which they can do from the trainer's own quest list.
A talk step is credited by a MarkTalked beat inside the conversation, never by pressing F, so
the trainer's dialogue carries one on the line the player picks. Re-point the step and that beat
has to move with it.
One mastery point is deliberate: it is enough to spend on the screen the quest just introduced,
so the first visit is not a locked door. Edit Rewards to re-tune it.
Requires.Quests names a quest the mod jar ships, which is what chains this pack onto the end of
the starter run; without the jar's temple quest finished the guide simply has nothing to offer.
The feature factor keeps the quest out of the log on a server with mastery switched off, where
the trainer never appears at all.
Listing.Hidden keeps it off open listings until it is taken; a giver always lists its own
quests, so the guide still offers it in the temple.
